--- title: "2 · The data" subtitle: "Two plain tables: daily weather and daily biomass" --- ```{=html}
You neednothing from earlier pages.You getthe two data frames used everywhere else, wx and traj.
``` ::: {.cell} ::: ## What the data are The data come from APSIM wheat simulations at **Narrabri**, a site in northern New South Wales: **199 genotypes** grown in **31 years** (1983 to 2013). Every genotype-year has daily biomass from 15 days after sowing until that genotype's own maturity. Because weather is the same for all genotypes in a given year, we keep weather and biomass in **separate tables**. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wx <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv") # one row per year x day traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz") # one row per genotype x year x day ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} head(wx, 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` year das TT DL RAW RAD 1 1983 15 247.50 11.191 0.7966 12 2 1983 16 256.75 11.180 0.7909 11 3 1983 17 267.50 11.169 0.7838 13 4 1983 18 278.00 11.158 0.7762 14 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(traj[traj$genotype == "g001" & traj$year == 1983, ], 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` genotype year das biomass lai 1 g001 1983 15 0.0164 0.039 2 g001 1983 16 0.0190 0.043 3 g001 1983 17 0.0228 0.049 4 g001 1983 18 0.0273 0.056 ``` ::: ::: | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | `das` | days after sowing (the data start at day 15) | | `TT` | thermal time: accumulated degree-days since sowing (°C d) | | `DL` | day length (h) | | `RAW` | relative available water, 0 (dry) to 1 (wet) | | `RAD` | solar radiation (MJ m⁻² d⁻¹) | | `biomass` | above-ground dry matter (t/ha) | | `lai` | leaf area index (m² m⁻²), used later | ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} c(genotypes = length(unique(traj$genotype)), years = length(unique(traj$year)), rows_weather = nrow(wx), rows_biomass = nrow(traj)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` genotypes years rows_weather rows_biomass 199 31 4453 849234 ``` ::: ::: ## Biomass trajectories Three genotypes in four different years. All genotypes follow the same season, but they differ in how fast they grow and when they finish. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sel <- traj[traj$genotype %in% c("g001", "g080", "g160") & traj$year %in% c(1984, 1990, 1998, 2008), ] ggplot(sel, aes(das, biomass, colour = genotype)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + facet_wrap(~year, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_manual(values = unname(dgxe[c("blue", "cyan", "orange")])) + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: ## The weather the crop experienced Four drivers over the same years. They look very different from year to year, and this variation is what lets us learn how growth responds to weather. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} w <- reshape(wx[wx$year %in% c(1984, 1990, 1998, 2008), ], direction = "long", varying = c("TT", "DL", "RAW", "RAD"), v.names = "value", timevar = "driver", times = c("TT", "DL", "RAW", "RAD"), idvar = c("year", "das")) w$driver <- factor(w$driver, c("TT", "DL", "RAW", "RAD")) ggplot(w, aes(das, value, colour = factor(year))) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~driver, scales = "free_y") + scale_colour_manual(values = unname(dgxe[c("blue", "cyan", "green", "orange")])) + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = NULL) + theme_dgxe() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-data_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Idea"} Two things to remember from this page. First, **weather is identical for all genotypes within a year**, so genotypes can only differ through the *coefficients* of the growth rule, not through their weather. Second, **thermal time keeps rising through the season**, so it also acts as a clock that tells the model how far along the crop is. ::: ::: {.callout-tip title="Check"} Do you get 199 genotypes and 31 years? Is the weather the same for every genotype? (It is: the weather table has no genotype column.) ::: ::: {.callout-important title="Pitfall"} Trajectories end on different days (each genotype matures at its own time). Keep track of where each one stops, as we do in the next step; padding with zeros or repeating the last value silently corrupts the regression. :::
